newsitem.title: CHINA: China to give preference to HK, European banks.
newsitem.headline: China to give preference to HK, European banks.

text.p: China will give preference to Hong Kong and European banks when selecting the next batch of foreign banks to be granted the right to conduct local currency business, the Business News said on Thursday.
The official newspaper said the central bank, which gave approval at the end of last month to four foreign banks to do yuan business, will approve more banks during 1997.
"People in financial circles predict that Hong Kong banks will receive preference, with European banks close behind them," it said.
The newspaper quoted an official from the People's Bank of China, the central bank, as saying the bank was considering applications received from many foreign banks to do local currency business.
It said the central bank wanted to encourage more foreign financial institutions to set up operations in inland areas of China, to help speed up economic development away from the coast.
The four banks so far approved to do yuan business in Shanghai on a trial basis are the Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corp, Citibank, Tokyo-Mitsubishi Bank and the Industrial Bank of Japan.
All foreign banks in China are restricted to doing business in foreign currency, but have been eager to gain a share of the huge local market for Chinese yuan deposits and loans.
According to rules issued last month, foreign banks wanting to do local currency business must move their Shanghai branches to the Pudong New Area to the east of the city centre.
